domain_label: Question & Answer Quality Evaluation (Question Science subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
evaluation is neutral and informational, scoring quality rather than enforcing any policy
a single evaluation session has access to the question, the answer(s), and the question under discussion
scores are relative and comparable within a session, not absolute ground-truth quality
exclusions: factual verification of claims against external ground truth (delegated to a fact-checking KB)
safety, policy, or content-moderation judgments beyond honesty/overclaim
model-internal or training-time evaluation; this is response-level scoring
automated answer generation or repair; this KB only scores
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for question-and-answer quality evaluation work units, informed by Gricean pragmatics, erotetic/answerhood theory, argumentation theory, IR relevance, and calibration research; no supplied dataset
source_citation: Grice 1975 Logic and Conversation (maxims of quantity, quality, relation, manner); Belnap & Steel 1976 The Logic of Questions and Answers (answerhood); Toulmin 1958 The Uses of Argument (grounds/warrant/backing); Tetlock & Gardner 2015 Superforecasting (calibration); van Rijsbergen 1979 Information Retrieval (topical relevance); Roberts 2012 Information Structure: Towards an Integrated Formal Theory of Pragmatics (question under discussion)

competency_questions.question: Is the question well-formed and are its presuppositions sound, so a true answer can exist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WELLFORMED and PRESUP_SOUNDNESS establish answerhood preconditions and presupposition truth

competency_questions.question: How is overall question quality scored and kept separate from answer quality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUESTION_QUALITY aggregates well-formedness, presupposition soundness, and answerability

competency_questions.question: How is the answer's relevance to the question under discussion judged?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RELEVANCE anchors topical relevance to an explicit QUD, gated by question quality

competency_questions.question: How are scope match and granularity match between question and answer checked?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SCOPE_MATCH and GRANULARITY_MATCH check requested breadth and detail level

competency_questions.question: How are directness and deflection/non-answers distinguished?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DIRECTNESS scores responsiveness; DEFLECTION_DETECT flags non-answers

competency_questions.question: How are the answer's informativeness and specificity scored?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INFORMATIVENESS scores uncertainty reduction per the Gricean quantity maxim

competency_questions.question: How are answer adequacy and multi-part coverage evaluated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANSWER_ADEQUACY judges completion; ANSWER_COVERAGE maps each sub-question

competency_questions.question: How is the evidential warrant linking grounds to claims evaluated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WARRANT_EVAL checks Toulmin warrant and backing for load-bearing claims

competency_questions.question: How are the answer's evidence tier and falsifiability assigned?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVIDENCE_TIER tiers support strength; FALSIFIABLE_CHECK finds confirm/refute paths

competency_questions.question: How are internal consistency and confidence calibration evaluated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSISTENCY detects contradictions; CALIBRATION scores confidence vs evidence

competency_questions.question: How is appropriate hedging distinguished from over- and under-hedging?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HEDGING_EVAL judges qualifiers against the evidence the answer cites

competency_questions.question: How are overclaim, under-support, and deflection detected?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OVERCLAIM_DETECT and DEFLECTION_DETECT separate overreach and evasion from honest answers

competency_questions.question: What multi-dimensional rubric and aggregation produce comparable scores?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTIDIM_RUBRIC defines anchored dimensions; RUBRIC_AGGREGATE combines them

competency_questions.question: How are candidate answers ranked comparably and consistently?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPARATIVE_RANK orders answers from rubric profiles with a transitivity check

glossary.definition: the proposition the current question requests an answer to, against which relevance and adequacy are judged
a response that supplies exactly the proposition the question requests, in Belnap & Steel's answerhood sense
a proposition taken for granted by a question or answer that must hold for it to be felicitous
the inference license, in Toulmin's terms, that moves from stated grounds to the asserted claim
an ordered label for the strength of support behind a claim, from unsourced assertion to primary evidence
the degree to which expressed confidence matches the actual likelihood the claim is correct given its evidence
an assertion whose strength exceeds what its warrant and evidence tier support
a response that avoids the requested proposition by switching, restating, or padding the question
a scoring instrument with named, level-anchored dimensions yielding a per-answer profile
the rule combining per-dimension sub-scores into one comparable score, including weights and vetoes

nodes.definition: Assess whether the question is well-formed: syntactically intelligible, semantically determinate, and carrying a satisfiable presupposition set, so that a true answer can exist at all (Belnap & Steel's answerhood preconditions).

base.update_signal: question grammar or answerhood preconditions revised

pros.claim: A well-formedness gate filters questions that admit no true answer before any answer scoring is attempted
pros.example: 'have you stopped overclaiming?' is flagged as carrying a false presupposition

cons.claim: Strict well-formedness can reject loosely phrased but genuinely answerable questions
cons.example: a colloquial 'why even bother?' rejected though its intent is recoverable

failure_modes: ambiguous question scored as if determinate
loaded question's false presupposition passes unflagged
acceptance_tests: question has a determinate reading and a satisfiable presupposition set

nodes.definition: Evaluate the soundness of the presuppositions the question and answer rely on: are the taken-for-granted propositions true and accepted in the discourse, distinguishing genuine information gaps from loaded or complex questions.

pros.claim: Separating a false presupposition from a real gap stops the evaluator from rewarding an answer that accepts a false premise
pros.example: an answer that 'corrects the question' scores higher than one that answers the loaded form

cons.claim: Presupposition analysis is context-sensitive; accommodation norms differ by discourse and can over-flag
cons.example: a domain term presupposed as shared is treated as a loaded premise

failure_modes: false presupposition accommodated silently
legitimate shared premise mis-flagged as loaded
acceptance_tests: presupposition truth and acceptance are explicitly checked before crediting the answer
revisit_triggers: a loaded question slipped through to scoring

nodes.definition: Produce an overall question-quality score combining well-formedness, presupposition soundness, specificity, and answerability, so questions can be compared and a poor question is not allowed to inflate or deflate the answer's evaluation.

pros.claim: Scoring the question itself prevents a vague prompt from being silently blamed on the answerer
pros.example: a one-word ambiguous prompt is marked low-quality, not the under-specified answer to it

cons.claim: A single question-quality number hides which dimension failed and can mislead downstream comparison
cons.example: two questions tie on the aggregate but fail for opposite reasons

failure_modes: poor question score conflated with poor answer
question quality scored on a hidden, non-reproducible rubric
acceptance_tests: question score decomposes into named sub-scores with reproducible weights

nodes.definition: Judge the answer's relevance to the question under discussion (QUD): does it address the proposition the question requests, in the sense of Grice's maxim of relation and IR topical relevance, rather than an adjacent or different question.

base.update_signal: QUD model or relevance criterion changes

pros.claim: Anchoring relevance to an explicit QUD makes 'off-topic' a checkable property rather than a reviewer impression
pros.example: an eloquent answer to a neighbouring question scores low on relevance to the asked QUD

cons.claim: QUD identification is itself interpretive; a mis-identified QUD makes every relevance judgment wrong
cons.example: reading the QUD too narrowly penalizes a correctly broad answer

failure_modes: answer scored relevant to a mis-identified QUD
topical overlap mistaken for genuine relevance
acceptance_tests: the QUD is stated explicitly and the answer is judged against it, not a paraphrase

nodes.definition: Check that the answer's scope matches the question's scope: neither narrower (leaving requested parts unanswered) nor broader (answering more than asked), so breadth is appropriate to the QUD.

pros.claim: Explicit scope matching separates 'answered too little' from 'answered too much', which a single relevance score conflates
pros.example: a question about one region answered for all regions is flagged as over-scope

cons.claim: Some questions legitimately invite scope expansion; rigid scope matching penalizes helpful context
cons.example: a 'what is X?' answer that adds a crucial caveat is dinged as over-scope

failure_modes: partial answer scored as complete
scope creep rewarded as thoroughness
acceptance_tests: answer breadth is mapped to the question's requested breadth with under/over-scope flags

nodes.definition: Check that the answer's granularity (level of detail/abstraction) matches what the question requests: a yes/no question should not require a treatise, and a how-question should not be answered with a one-word label.

pros.claim: Granularity matching distinguishes an appropriately concise answer from an evasively shallow one
pros.example: a one-line answer to a yes/no question is correct, not penalized as thin

cons.claim: Granularity preferences vary by audience; a fixed target mis-serves experts and novices alike
cons.example: an expert audience finds the 'right' granularity patronizing

failure_modes: concise correct answer penalized as shallow
verbose padding rewarded as depth
acceptance_tests: answer detail level is compared to the question's requested granularity

nodes.definition: Assess how directly the answer responds to the question: does it lead with the requested proposition (a direct answer in Belnap & Steel's sense) or bury/withhold it behind preamble, qualification, or redirection.

base.update_signal: directness rubric or hedging policy changes

pros.claim: Measuring directness catches answers that technically contain the information but withhold it behind evasion
pros.example: the answer is in the last sentence after three paragraphs of hedging, flagged as low-directness

cons.claim: Maximal directness can punish answers whose honest uncertainty genuinely requires qualification first
cons.example: a correctly cautious 'it depends, because...' reads as indirect

failure_modes: evasive answer scored as responsive
necessary qualification mistaken for evasion
acceptance_tests: the requested proposition is locatable and its position/prominence in the answer is scored

nodes.definition: Score the answer's informativeness and specificity: how much it reduces the questioner's uncertainty, per Grice's maxim of quantity (as informative as required, not more), favouring specific commitments over vacuous generality.

base.update_signal: informativeness measure or quantity-maxim policy changes

pros.claim: Rewarding specific, uncertainty-reducing content separates a substantive answer from a fluent non-answer
pros.example: 'about 40%' is more informative than 'a significant portion', other things equal

cons.claim: Maximizing informativeness pushes toward over-commitment beyond what the evidence warrants
cons.example: a precise number is asserted where only a range is supported

failure_modes: vacuous generality scored as informative
spurious precision rewarded over warranted hedging
acceptance_tests: informativeness is scored as uncertainty reduction relative to what the question asked

nodes.definition: Evaluate adequacy: whether the answer fully resolves the question it addresses, completing the proposition the question requested rather than partially or tangentially touching it (answerhood completeness).

pros.claim: Adequacy makes 'fully answered' a checkable property distinct from 'said something relevant'
pros.example: a partial answer that resolves one of two requested facts is marked adequate-partial, not adequate

cons.claim: Adequacy can demand more than a hard question admits, penalizing honest partial answers to open problems
cons.example: an answer to a genuinely unresolved question is dinged for incompleteness

failure_modes: partial answer scored as fully adequate
open-problem answer over-penalized for incompleteness
acceptance_tests: the answer is judged complete or partial against the explicit requested proposition
revisit_triggers: adequacy dispute on an open question

nodes.definition: Decompose a complex/multi-part question into its sub-questions and verify coverage: each sub-question is mapped to at least one part of the answer, so a multi-part question is not scored on a single salient part.

pros.claim: Sub-question coverage catches the common failure where a multi-part question is answered only in its easy part
pros.example: a 'what and why' question answered only on 'what' is flagged as 50% coverage

cons.claim: Sub-question decomposition is interpretive; over-splitting invents obligations the asker did not intend
cons.example: a single intent is split into three pedantic sub-questions

failure_modes: multi-part question scored on one part
over-decomposition fabricates uncovered sub-questions
acceptance_tests: each identified sub-question maps to a covering answer span or an explicit gap
revisit_triggers: a multi-part question mis-scored on one part

nodes.definition: Evaluate the evidential warrant linking the answer's claims to its grounds, in Toulmin's sense: is there a stated or recoverable warrant that licenses moving from the cited grounds to the asserted claim, with backing where needed.

base.update_signal: warrant model or backing requirement changes

pros.claim: A Toulmin warrant check exposes claims that assert a conclusion without licensing the inference from their grounds
pros.example: an answer cites a correlation as grounds for a causal claim with no warrant, flagged

cons.claim: Demanding explicit warrant penalizes correct answers in domains where the inference is conventionally tacit
cons.example: a textbook fact is dinged for not re-deriving its warrant

failure_modes: unwarranted leap from grounds to claim accepted
tacit but valid warrant treated as missing
acceptance_tests: each load-bearing claim has a recoverable warrant linking it to stated grounds

nodes.definition: Assign an evidence tier to the answer's support: from unsourced assertion, through cited secondary source, to primary/observed/experimental evidence, so the strength of grounds is explicit and comparable across answers.

pros.claim: An explicit evidence tier makes 'better supported' comparable across answers instead of an impression
pros.example: an answer citing a primary measurement outranks one asserting the same claim unsourced

cons.claim: Tier labels can be gamed by citing weak sources that look authoritative
cons.example: a citation to an irrelevant but prestigious source inflates the tier

failure_modes: unsourced assertion tiered as evidenced
prestige source mistaken for relevant evidence
acceptance_tests: the answer's support is mapped to an explicit, ordered evidence tier

nodes.definition: Determine whether the answer's claims are falsifiable/checkable: is there a stated or implied way to confirm or refute them, distinguishing testable commitments from unfalsifiable, self-sealing, or purely rhetorical statements.

pros.claim: A falsifiability check separates a checkable commitment from an unfalsifiable hedge that cannot be wrong
pros.example: 'it may or may not rain' is flagged as unfalsifiable, not credited as cautious

cons.claim: Some valid normative or definitional answers are legitimately not empirically falsifiable
cons.example: a definitional answer is wrongly penalized for non-testability

failure_modes: unfalsifiable hedge scored as a safe answer
valid definitional claim penalized as untestable
acceptance_tests: each empirical claim has a stated or implied confirm/refute path
revisit_triggers: an unfalsifiable claim was credited as cautious

nodes.definition: Check the answer's internal consistency: it must not assert mutually contradictory propositions, and its stated confidence, scope, and conclusions must cohere across the whole response.

pros.claim: Internal-consistency checking catches answers that hedge then assert, or contradict themselves across sections
pros.example: an answer says 'unknown' then later asserts the unknown value, flagged

cons.claim: Apparent contradictions can be context-shifted distinctions that surface checking would over-flag
cons.example: two claims true under different stated conditions read as a contradiction

failure_modes: self-contradiction passes unflagged
legitimate context-shift mis-flagged as contradiction
acceptance_tests: the answer is free of unresolved internal contradictions across claims, scope, and confidence

nodes.definition: Evaluate calibration: whether the answer's expressed confidence matches the strength of its evidence and warrant, rewarding stated confidence that tracks reality (Tetlock-style calibration) and penalizing both over- and under-confidence.

pros.claim: Calibration scoring makes confidence accountable to evidence, the way proper scoring rules reward honest probabilities
pros.example: a 'probably' backed by strong evidence outscores a 'certainly' backed by weak grounds

cons.claim: Calibration pressure can push answers toward bland mid-confidence that is hard to mark wrong
cons.example: every answer hedges to 'maybe' to dodge a calibration penalty

failure_modes: confident wrong answer rewarded for fluency
honest hedging penalized as low confidence
acceptance_tests: expressed confidence is scored against evidence strength, penalizing over- and under-confidence
revisit_triggers: systematic over/under-confidence observed in scored answers

nodes.definition: Evaluate hedging quality: whether qualifiers, ranges, and uncertainty markers are used where and only where the evidence warrants them, distinguishing honest, informative hedging from both evasive over-hedging and reckless under-hedging.

pros.claim: Scoring hedging quality rewards a qualifier that carries real information and penalizes one that only dodges commitment
pros.example: 'between 30 and 50%' informs; 'some unknown amount' merely hedges

cons.claim: Hedging norms are audience- and stakes-dependent; a fixed standard mis-serves high- and low-stakes contexts
cons.example: cautious clinical phrasing reads as evasive in a casual context

failure_modes: evasive over-hedging scored as appropriate caution
reckless under-hedging scored as confidence
acceptance_tests: each qualifier is judged warranted, over-hedged, or under-hedged against the evidence

nodes.definition: Detect overclaim and under-support: assertions whose strength exceeds their warrant and evidence tier, including spurious precision, unsupported universals, and causal claims from correlational grounds.

pros.claim: Overclaim detection penalizes the confident-but-unsupported answer that informativeness scoring alone would reward
pros.example: 'always' is flagged where the grounds support only 'often')

cons.claim: Aggressive overclaim flags can suppress legitimately strong claims that do have adequate warrant
cons.example: a well-supported strong claim is dinged as overclaim by an over-sensitive flag

failure_modes: overclaim rewarded as confident expertise
well-warranted strong claim suppressed as overclaim
acceptance_tests: each claim's asserted strength is checked against its warrant and evidence tier
revisit_triggers: an overclaim was credited as strong evidence

nodes.definition: Detect deflection and non-answers: responses that change the question, answer a different (easier) question, restate the question, or fill space without committing to the requested proposition.

pros.claim: Deflection detection catches the fluent non-answer that scores well on tone but never commits to the requested proposition
pros.example: a polished response that answers an adjacent question is flagged as a non-answer

cons.claim: A genuine 'I cannot answer, and here is why' is a legitimate response that crude deflection flags over-penalize
cons.example: an honest, well-reasoned refusal is mis-flagged as evasion

failure_modes: fluent non-answer scored as a real answer
honest justified refusal mis-flagged as deflection
acceptance_tests: the response is checked for whether it commits to the requested proposition or deflects
revisit_triggers: a non-answer was scored as an answer

nodes.definition: Define the multi-dimensional rubric: the named, anchored dimensions (relevance, informativeness, adequacy, warrant, calibration, honesty) with level descriptors, so each answer receives a transparent per-dimension profile, not a single opaque score.

pros.claim: An anchored multi-dimensional rubric makes scores reproducible and reveals which dimension drove a verdict
pros.example: two answers tie on total but the rubric shows one failed warrant and the other failed relevance

cons.claim: More dimensions raise annotation cost and inter-rater variance, and tempt double-counting correlated dimensions
cons.example: relevance and adequacy partly overlap, inflating a low score on both

failure_modes: dimensions overlap and double-count
unanchored levels yield non-reproducible scores
acceptance_tests: each dimension has level-anchored descriptors and produces an independent sub-score
revisit_triggers: inter-rater disagreement on a dimension rises

nodes.definition: Specify the aggregation policy that combines per-dimension sub-scores into a comparable overall score, including weights, any gating/veto dimensions, and how missing or not-applicable dimensions are handled, while preserving the underlying profile.

base.update_signal: aggregation weights or gating policy changes

pros.claim: A stated aggregation policy makes the overall score reproducible and lets a critical dimension veto rather than be averaged away
pros.example: a deflection veto caps the total regardless of fluent informativeness

cons.claim: Any aggregation discards information; a single number can hide a profile that two answers do not actually share
cons.example: two answers reach 0.7 by averaging opposite strengths and weaknesses

failure_modes: critical failure averaged away into a passing total
aggregate reported without the profile it came from
acceptance_tests: aggregation weights and any veto rules are explicit; the overall score ships with its profile
revisit_triggers: an averaged total masked a critical failure

nodes.definition: Rank candidate answers to the same question against each other using the rubric profiles and aggregation, producing a consistent, transitive ordering that is robust to irrelevant alternatives where possible.

base.update_signal: ranking method or transitivity policy changes

pros.claim: Comparative ranking is often more reliable than absolute scores because raters compare more consistently than they calibrate absolutely
pros.example: reviewers agree A beats B even when they disagree on A's absolute score

cons.claim: Pairwise preferences can be intransitive and order-sensitive, producing cycles or unstable rankings
cons.example: A>B, B>C, C>A cycle from inconsistent pairwise judgments

failure_modes: intransitive ranking cycle produced
ranking sensitive to the set of candidates compared
acceptance_tests: the ranking is checked for transitivity and ties are broken by named dimensions
revisit_triggers: a ranking cycle or instability observed

edges.why_related: sub-question coverage is an obligation the aggregation must reflect, not average away
granularity mismatch bounds how adequate an otherwise complete answer can be
hedging quality and overclaim are dual views of confidence-vs-evidence fit
overclaim and deflection are the two honesty failure poles the rubric must both catch
unfalsifiable claims cannot be calibrated, so falsifiability feeds calibration scoring
a low evidence tier under a strong claim is the signature of overclaim
an answer that exploits a false presupposition is a form of deflection to flag back
ranking disagreements feed back to refine ambiguous rubric anchors

edges.resolution_rule: cap informativeness credit at the warranted evidence tier: reward specificity only up to the point the evidence supports; beyond that, calibration and overclaim penalties dominate
edges.why_related: maximizing informativeness/specificity pushes toward claims stronger than the evidence warrants, which calibration penalizes
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: require the direct answer to lead, but do not penalize qualifiers that carry warranted, decision-relevant uncertainty; only evasive over-hedging reduces directness
edges.why_related: demanding a direct lead-with-the-answer response conflicts with honest hedging that genuine uncertainty requires
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: always ship the per-dimension profile alongside the aggregate, and let critical dimensions veto rather than average, so the single score never replaces the transparent profile
edges.why_related: collapsing the multi-dimensional profile into one aggregate score trades transparency for comparability
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

edges.resolution_rule: for hard or open questions, score warrant and adequacy on a curve relative to what is knowable: a well-warranted partial answer outranks an unwarranted complete-sounding one
edges.why_related: a strict warrant requirement can make hard but legitimately answerable questions look inadequate, penalizing honest partial answers
edges.benefit_of_coupling: tension surfaced and resolved by rule

conflict_axes.name: informativeness_vs_calibration
conflict_axes.description: Rewarding specific, uncertainty-reducing answers pushes toward commitments stronger than the evidence warrants; calibration and overclaim detection pull the other way.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: credit specificity only up to the warranted evidence tier

conflict_axes.name: directness_vs_honest_hedging
conflict_axes.description: Demanding a direct lead-with-the-answer response competes with the qualification honest uncertainty requires.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: penalize only evasive over-hedging, not warranted decision-relevant uncertainty

conflict_axes.name: single_aggregate_vs_multidim_transparency
conflict_axes.description: A single comparable score is convenient but hides which dimension drove the verdict; the full profile is transparent but harder to rank.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: ship the profile with the aggregate; use vetoes not averaging for critical dimensions

conflict_axes.name: strict_warrant_vs_answering_hard_questions
conflict_axes.description: A strict warrant/evidence requirement penalizes honest partial answers to genuinely hard or open questions.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: score warrant and adequacy on a curve relative to what is knowable

conflict_axes.name: scope_breadth_vs_focus
conflict_axes.description: Broad answers cover more of a multi-part question but risk over-scope and dilution; focused answers are crisp but may under-cover.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: match scope to the QUD's requested breadth; reward coverage only of asked parts

conflict_axes.name: specificity_vs_falsifiability_safety
conflict_axes.description: More specific claims are more informative but also more falsifiable and thus riskier; vague claims are safe but uninformative.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reward specific falsifiable claims while pricing in their error risk via calibration

conflict_axes.name: relevance_strictness_vs_helpful_context
conflict_axes.description: Strict QUD relevance penalizes added context; lenient relevance rewards tangents that pad the answer.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: credit context only when it materially serves the QUD; flag the rest as over-scope

conflict_axes.name: granularity_for_experts_vs_novices
conflict_axes.description: The right level of detail differs by audience, so a fixed granularity target mis-serves some readers.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: score granularity against the question's stated or inferred audience, not a fixed level

conflict_axes.name: deflection_flagging_vs_honest_refusal
conflict_axes.description: Aggressive deflection detection risks penalizing a legitimate, well-reasoned 'I cannot answer, and here is why'.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: distinguish a justified refusal with reasons from an evasive non-answer

edge_cases.description: A loaded question with a false presupposition is answered on its own terms, rewarding an answer that accepts the false premise.
edge_cases.trigger: presupposition soundness not checked before scoring the answer
edge_cases.mitigation: flag the false presupposition; credit answers that correct rather than accept it

edge_cases.description: A fluent, confident answer to a neighbouring question scores high on tone but never addresses the actual QUD.
edge_cases.trigger: relevance judged against a paraphrased rather than explicit QUD
edge_cases.mitigation: state the QUD explicitly and score relevance and deflection against it

edge_cases.description: An answer asserts spurious precision (a sharp number) where the evidence supports only a range, and informativeness scoring rewards it.
edge_cases.trigger: informativeness credited without checking warrant and evidence tier
edge_cases.mitigation: cap informativeness at the warranted tier; apply an overclaim penalty

edge_cases.description: A multi-part question is answered only in its easy part, and the salient part dominates the score.
edge_cases.trigger: sub-question coverage not computed for a complex question
edge_cases.mitigation: decompose into sub-questions and require each to map to a covering span or gap

edge_cases.description: An answer hedges everything to 'maybe' to dodge a calibration penalty, sacrificing all informativeness.
edge_cases.trigger: calibration penalty applied without rewarding warranted specificity
edge_cases.mitigation: reward hedging only when warranted; penalize evasive over-hedging via directness

edge_cases.description: A causal claim is asserted from purely correlational grounds with no warrant, but reads as authoritative.
edge_cases.trigger: warrant from grounds to claim not evaluated
edge_cases.mitigation: require a recoverable warrant; flag correlation-to-causation leaps as overclaim

edge_cases.description: An unfalsifiable, self-sealing statement is scored as a safe, cautious answer.
edge_cases.trigger: falsifiability not checked, so a non-committal claim looks prudent
edge_cases.mitigation: flag self-sealing statements as unfalsifiable, not as warranted caution

edge_cases.description: The aggregate score averages a critical deflection failure away into a passing total.
edge_cases.trigger: aggregation averages a veto-worthy dimension instead of gating on it
edge_cases.mitigation: let critical dimensions veto the total; always ship the profile with the score

edge_cases.description: Pairwise answer comparisons produce an intransitive cycle (A>B>C>A), so no consistent ranking exists.
edge_cases.trigger: ranking taken from inconsistent pairwise judgments without a transitivity check
edge_cases.mitigation: check transitivity; resolve cycles by aggregating dimension sub-scores

edge_cases.description: An honest, well-reasoned refusal ('I cannot answer because the data does not exist') is mis-flagged as deflection.
edge_cases.trigger: deflection detection ignores justified refusals with stated reasons
edge_cases.mitigation: credit a refusal that gives warranted reasons; reserve deflection for evasion

edge_cases.description: An answer correct at expert granularity is penalized as too terse for a novice question, or vice versa.
edge_cases.trigger: granularity scored against a fixed level instead of the question's audience
edge_cases.mitigation: score granularity against the question's stated or inferred audience

edge_cases.description: An answer contradicts itself across sections (declares 'unknown' then asserts the value), yet scores well on each part in isolation.
edge_cases.trigger: internal consistency not checked across the whole response
edge_cases.mitigation: run a whole-response contradiction check before crediting any claim

workflow.description: Verify the question is intelligible, determinate, and carries satisfiable presuppositions before any answer scoring.
workflow.gate: question has a determinate reading and satisfiable presuppositions

workflow.description: Evaluate the truth and acceptance of the question's and answer's presuppositions; flag loaded/complex questions.
Aggregate well-formedness, presupposition soundness, specificity, and answerability into a question-quality score with named sub-scores.
workflow.gate: question score decomposes into reproducible sub-scores

workflow.description: State the QUD explicitly and judge the answer's topical relevance to it.
workflow.gate: QUD stated; answer judged against it

workflow.description: Map answer breadth and detail level to the question's requested scope and granularity, flagging under/over.
Locate the requested proposition and score how directly and prominently the answer supplies it.
workflow.gate: requested proposition located and its prominence scored

workflow.description: Score uncertainty reduction and specificity, then adequacy and sub-question coverage.
Check the warrant from grounds to claims, assign an evidence tier, and test falsifiability.
workflow.gate: each load-bearing claim has a warrant and evidence tier

workflow.description: Score confidence calibration, hedging quality, overclaim, and deflection against the evidence.
workflow.gate: confidence scored vs evidence; overclaim and deflection flagged

workflow.description: Record the per-dimension, level-anchored sub-scores into a transparent answer profile.
workflow.gate: each dimension has an independent anchored sub-score

workflow.description: Combine sub-scores with explicit weights and vetoes, shipping the profile alongside the aggregate.
Rank candidate answers from their rubric profiles and check the ordering for transitivity.
workflow.gate: ranking is transitive; ties broken by named dimensions

dominance_rules.rule: WELLFORMED and PRESUP_SOUNDNESS must pass before any answer dimension is scored
dominance_rules.rationale: scoring an answer to an ill-formed or loaded question conflates question and answer defects
dominance_rules.trigger: answer scoring begins on an unchecked question
dominance_rules.action: block answer scoring until the question is well-formed and its presuppositions checked

dominance_rules.rule: RELEVANCE to an explicit QUD must be established before informativeness, adequacy, or warrant are credited
dominance_rules.rationale: informative, well-warranted content about the wrong question is still a non-answer
dominance_rules.trigger: content dimensions scored without a stated QUD
dominance_rules.action: require an explicit QUD and an on-question relevance judgment first

dominance_rules.rule: INFORMATIVENESS credit must be capped at the warranted evidence tier
dominance_rules.rationale: rewarding specificity beyond the evidence incentivizes overclaim
dominance_rules.trigger: a precise claim scored informative above its evidence tier
dominance_rules.action: cap informativeness at the warranted tier and apply the overclaim penalty

dominance_rules.rule: DEFLECTION_DETECT must distinguish a justified refusal from an evasive non-answer
dominance_rules.rationale: penalizing honest 'cannot answer, here is why' responses rewards confident guessing
dominance_rules.trigger: a refusal with stated reasons flagged as deflection
dominance_rules.action: credit warranted refusals; reserve the deflection flag for evasion

dominance_rules.rule: RUBRIC_AGGREGATE must ship the per-dimension profile and let critical dimensions veto
dominance_rules.rationale: averaging hides a critical failure behind a passing total
dominance_rules.trigger: an aggregate reported without its profile or with a critical failure averaged away
dominance_rules.action: attach the profile and gate on veto dimensions

dominance_rules.rule: WARRANT_EVAL and ANSWER_ADEQUACY must be scored relative to what is knowable for hard questions
dominance_rules.rationale: a strict absolute standard penalizes honest partial answers to open problems
dominance_rules.trigger: an open-question answer marked inadequate against a closed-question standard
dominance_rules.action: score warrant and adequacy on a knowability-relative curve

dominance_rules.rule: CONSISTENCY must be checked across the whole response before any claim is credited
dominance_rules.rationale: a self-contradictory answer can score well on each part in isolation
dominance_rules.trigger: per-part scoring without a whole-response contradiction check
dominance_rules.action: run a whole-response consistency check first

dominance_rules.rule: COMPARATIVE_RANK must verify transitivity before publishing an ordering
dominance_rules.rationale: intransitive pairwise preferences yield an undefined ranking
dominance_rules.trigger: a ranking derived from inconsistent pairwise judgments
dominance_rules.action: check transitivity and resolve cycles via dimension sub-scores

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not score answer dimensions before the question is well-formed and its presuppositions checked; question defects otherwise contaminate answer scores
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-scoring every answer after discovering the question was loaded

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not judge relevance against a paraphrased QUD; fixing a mis-identified QUD invalidates all dependent scores
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-running the full rubric after the QUD is corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not credit informativeness above the warranted evidence tier; retracting inflated scores after an overclaim is found is costly
anti_rework_rules.prevents: reworking informativeness and calibration scores after an overclaim audit

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not collapse the rubric to a single number without retaining the profile; reconstructing dimension scores later is expensive
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-annotating answers to recover a discarded per-dimension profile

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not finalize calibration before falsifiability is checked; an unfalsifiable claim cannot be calibrated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-doing calibration after discovering a claim was self-sealing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not flag deflection without checking for a justified refusal; reversing a wrong deflection flag means re-scoring honesty
anti_rework_rules.prevents: honesty re-scoring after a refusal was mis-flagged as evasion

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not rank answers before checking transitivity; an intransitive ranking must be discarded and rebuilt
anti_rework_rules.prevents: republishing a ranking after a cycle is detected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Do not aggregate before sub-question coverage is computed for complex questions; a missing sub-question surfaces as a late coverage gap
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-aggregating after a multi-part question is found under-covered

iteration_protocol.trigger: a loaded or ill-formed question reaches answer scoring unflagged
iteration_protocol.action: tighten WELLFORMED and PRESUP_SOUNDNESS gates and re-run question-quality scoring

iteration_protocol.trigger: a fluent non-answer to a neighbouring question scores high
iteration_protocol.action: make the QUD explicit in RELEVANCE and strengthen DEFLECTION_DETECT

iteration_protocol.trigger: a confident but under-supported answer outscores a warranted hedged one
iteration_protocol.action: cap INFORMATIVENESS at the evidence tier and strengthen CALIBRATION and OVERCLAIM_DETECT

iteration_protocol.trigger: a multi-part question is scored on only its easy part
iteration_protocol.action: enforce sub-question decomposition in ANSWER_COVERAGE and gate ANSWER_ADEQUACY on it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a critical failure is averaged into a passing aggregate
iteration_protocol.action: add a veto for the critical dimension in RUBRIC_AGGREGATE and attach the MULTIDIM_RUBRIC profile

iteration_protocol.trigger: an honest justified refusal is mis-flagged as deflection
iteration_protocol.action: refine DEFLECTION_DETECT to credit warranted refusals using WARRANT_EVAL

iteration_protocol.trigger: a comparative ranking produces an intransitive cycle
iteration_protocol.action: add a transitivity check in COMPARATIVE_RANK and resolve via RUBRIC_AGGREGATE sub-scores

priority_rationale: WELLFORMED, PRESUP_SOUNDNESS, and QUESTION_QUALITY gate the question; RELEVANCE anchors every answer dimension; content (informativeness/adequacy/coverage) and evidence (warrant/tier/falsifiability/consistency) feed honesty (calibration/hedging/overclaim/deflection); the multi-dimensional rubric, aggregation, and ranking close the method last.
